title: sources (widget tool input)
description: What the agent sends to the widget tool: the payload without id, rev and producer (the tool sets them); fallback_text optional (the tool writes it); from_file allowed. The references behind an answer, numbered to match [1] markers in the prose and tagged with how far to trust them; one source with an excerpt renders as a quote.

title.description: The page, document or post title as published.

url.description: Where it is. The row shows the domain taken from this URL by the client (never from the payload’s words) and opens it after showing the domain.

site.description: The publisher, when there’s no URL or the domain doesn’t say who it is: “EU Official Journal”, “Financial Times (print)”.

kind.description: What kind of source it is. Read by VoiceOver, and a guide to `trust`: official, research, docs and data are usually primary; press secondary; forum and social unverified until something primary confirms them.

trust.description: How far to trust it, as the row’s tag: primary (“Primary source”, green), secondary (grey), unverified (dashed outline with a question mark, never green), retracted (red; the title turns secondary). Required.

published.description: When it was published (or last updated). Shown after the domain: “14 Oct”.

note.description: Replaces the domain line when what the source is needs saying: “A post on X, not confirmed”. The domain still shows before the link opens.

excerpt.description: The passage the answer relies on, quoted exactly, never paraphrased. One source with an excerpt renders as a quote.

locator.description: Where in the source: “Article 111”, “p. 14”, “at 12:40”. Part of the quote’s attribution.

used_for.description: What the answer took from it: “The 2027 deadline”. A caption under the row.

actions.description: Up to two row actions, such as Check This on an unverified source. They send `{item: <id>}`; `id` is then required.

items.description: The sources, in the order the reply numbers them: [1] is the first. An empty list only to say the answer has none.

layout.description: auto: one item with an excerpt renders as a quote, anything else as a list. quote needs exactly one item with an excerpt.
